title: Annex to the Renew Business Asset Buyback Agreement: Consent to a Collection Run
content:
**A1. Collection in runs.** A Renew Business Asset Buyback agreement is collected in runs, and the machines one run carries are settled with the customer before the customer consents to the handover.

**A2. When a run may be settled.** The machines of a run are settled only while the agreement is still waiting for machines to be collected and none has been booked in on it.

**A3. An agreement that runs out.** An agreement the customer has accepted runs out where the machines never reach the retailer, the day it runs out being recorded on the agreement as the day its quote ran out, and no run is settled on it thereafter.

**A4. The consent itself.** The consent to hand machines to the retailer's freight carrier is the customer's own, the machines being the customer's property. It is asked for when the business buyer asks for a collection to be arranged, and once it is on record the carrier can be sent for those machines.

**A5. What the consent puts on record.** A fresh collection record, which is the shipment request the machines are to travel on, is opened against the agreement carrying the day asked for, the machines the consent covers, freight collection as the way the machines travel, and the consent itself marked as given by the customer. The agreement is also set to travel by freight collection, which is the choice the customer is making. The consent covers both handing the stated number of machines over on the day the customer names and the destruction of the data on those machines once they are in the retailer's hands.

**A6. Recording the consent.** The record is made through `confirm_handover_units_5801b6db`. Because the act is the customer's, the tool is unlocked for the customer and handed over, and the customer themselves runs it; it is not run for them.

**A7. What the record takes.**

| What is given | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `tradein_agreement_id` | Id class — the reference number of the Renew trade-in agreement the machines are traded under, read from the trade-in agreement record found for the customer profile. |
| `customer_id` | Id class — the customer reference number of the profile trading the machines in, read from the customer profile record. |
| `requested_collection_date` | Fixed-format class — the day the customer asks for the machines to be collected, written as YYYY-MM-DD in the retailer's local calendar date, with no time part; it is never left empty. |
| `units_declared` | Fixed-format class — how many machines the customer consents to hand over on this run, as a whole count of machines with no decimal part and never below zero. |

**A8. What comes back.** A confirmation line in plain text naming the collection record opened, the agreement it belongs to, the day asked for, the whole count of machines the consent covers and the way the machines will travel. The line being returned is what shows the consent is on record, and the run can then be read back on the agreement's collection records, with the agreement itself showing freight collection as the way the machines will travel.
